SOC Automation & Orchestration.

I built n8n workflows that connect Wazuh alerts with SOC notifications, risk-based escalation, DFIR-IRIS case management, and investigation handoffs.

SOC alert orchestration 3D visualization

Wazuh → n8n normalization → triage → DFIR-IRIS correlation → conditional IOC synchronization → SOC-03 investigation handoff. A separate branch handles SOC email notification.

The animation represents an illustrative workflow, not actual live alert processing or an execution trace. Drag horizontally to rotate, or use the arrow keys. Press Home to reset the view.

  1. Wazuh generates a security alert.
  2. n8n receives and normalizes the event.
  3. Severity and escalation rules are evaluated.
  4. DFIR-IRIS alerts and cases are correlated.
  5. IOC synchronization occurs when allowed and needed.
  6. Investigation context may be handed to the downstream SOC-03 workflow.
  7. High- and critical-severity notifications are handled on a separate email branch.

What I Built

Alert Processing

Developed Wazuh webhook intake, event normalization, severity filtering, IOC extraction and SOC email notifications.

Escalation Decisions

Implemented policy-based scoring using security indicators, MITRE ATT&CK context, suppression flags and alert severity.

Incident Orchestration

Built DFIR-IRIS lookups, case correlation, duplicate checks, conditional writes, IOC handling and downstream handoff logic.

What I Learned

Building this workflow taught me how data quality, API reliability, correlation and controlled escalation affect SOC automation. It also reinforced the importance of keeping analysts involved when an alert needs human judgment.

Evidence

The 3D model illustrates the workflow architecture, not live SOC activity. The supplied workflow exports cover Wazuh, n8n, DFIR-IRIS and a downstream investigation handoff. OpenCTI is part of the wider tool integration context; completed OpenCTI enrichment is not demonstrated by these two exports.
